title: Port Harcourt refinery repair
source: NNPC's own money, the federal budget and an Afreximbank loan
simple: In 2021 the government approved $1.5 billion to repair the old Port Harcourt refinery so Nigeria could make its own fuel. It restarted in late 2024, was shut for maintenance in May 2025, and in 2026 it was still not working steadily.

verdict.text: Restarted in Nov 2024, then shut for maintenance in May 2025
How much of the $1.5 billion was spent, and on what: no public breakdown found

summary: In March 2021 the Federal Executive Council approved $1.5 billion to repair the Port Harcourt refinery, and the Italian firm Tecnimont was hired to do the work. The money was to come from NNPC's own revenue, the federal budget and a loan arranged with Afreximbank. NNPC restarted the older plant (60,000 barrels a day) in November 2024 and announced a maintenance shutdown from 24 May 2025. In February 2026 the oil workers' union PENGASSAN said the plant was about 90% repaired and could restart within a week, while NNPC said a restart had to make commercial sense.
gaps: We found no public breakdown of how much of the $1.5 billion has been spent, or how much came from each source (NNPC, the budget and Afreximbank).
We found no regular public reports of how much fuel the refinery has produced.
We could not confirm the refinery's exact state in November 2026.

timeline.text: The Federal Executive Council approves $1.5 billion to repair the refinery.
The repair contract is signed with Tecnimont.
NNPC restarts the older plant (60,000 barrels a day).
NNPC announces a planned maintenance shutdown, expected to last about a month.
The oil workers' union says the plant is 90% repaired and could restart within a week. NNPC says a restart must make commercial sense.
